name: Acetyl hexapeptide-38 (Sculptessence/Matrixyl 3000 relative)

lead:
Acetyl hexapeptide-38 is a cosmetic ingredient sold as Adifyline. Its supplier says it raises PGC-1 alpha in fat precursor cells, encouraging fat-cell formation and lipid storage, so that topical products can add volume to areas such as cheeks.
The appearance payoff claimed is a fuller, plumper face or lip contour without injection. The data published are supplier tests rather than independent trials.

paras: It is used as an ingredient in creams and serums applied to the face or lips, usually in volumizing or lip-care formulations.
It is a cosmetic ingredient with no published safety trials; as with any topical, skin reactions are possible. Claims for lips have no specific test described.

angle.text: The ingredient is marketed for adding soft-tissue volume to the face and lips with a topical product. Reported results come from supplier tests on cheeks and breasts.

lead: Acetyl hexapeptide-38, marketed as Adifyline, is a cosmetic peptide described by its supplier as a volume-enhancing, anti-ageing ingredient. It is said to increase expression of PGC-1 alpha, a coactivator that works with PPAR gamma in adipocyte differentiation, stimulating adipogenesis and lipid storage [1].

Users on looksmaxxing forums discuss it as a topical filler alternative for cheeks and lips. A 2011 trade article reports laboratory results in human preadipocytes and two panels of 22 women, one on cheeks for 14 days and one on breasts for 56 days [1].
No independent peer-reviewed trial is cited, and the trade article does not name the developing company [1].

paras: The 2011 trade article groups Adifyline with Silusyne (acetyl hexapeptide-39), which is said to do the opposite by lowering PGC-1 alpha for slimming [1].

In human subcutaneous preadipocytes over 10 days, Adifyline raised PGC-1 alpha expression by 25.6 percent at 0.1 mg/ml and 61.1 percent at 0.5 mg/ml, and lipid accumulation by 27.9 and 32.4 percent. In a 14-day cheek panel of women aged 50 to 60, volume rose 11.9 percent from baseline and 79 percent noticed visible enhancement. The article also reports a large breast-volume gain versus placebo over 56 days [1].

It appears in forum guides on topical fillers, usually alongside other volumizing actives, and is described as a non-injectable option for lips and cheeks. These posts are user accounts rather than trial data.
The only human data located are the supplier panels reported in a promotional trade article; no independent peer-reviewed human study was found, and no lip-specific test was identified [1].

timeline.event: Trade article reports in vitro and panel results for Adifyline [1]
